title: Wave orchestrator and safe-revert proxy for private installer
author: Maya Kline
release_notes: Introduces a coordinated 'upgrade wave' orchestrator for tenant-aware upgrades; adds a safe-revert proxy that enables low-risk network switchbacks during reverts; Helm hooks and Terraform plan gating to prevent partial upgrades; new preflight snapshot and ephemeral restore sandbox; downgrade guard checks to block incompatible version rollbacks; no user-facing API change.
description:
Context and motivation: private deployments need an automated, low-blast-radius path for staged upgrades and reverts. Customers operating multi-tenant private clusters asked for safer wave-based rollouts and deterministic revert behavior when a post-upgrade regression appears. This PR implements a wave orchestrator that sequences tenant groups, ensures pre-upgrade snapshots, and provides an automated safe-revert proxy that flips network traffic without performing destructive DB downgrades.

What this changes: high-level: 1) wave orchestrator service (k8s operator) that consumes a release plan and coordinates per-tenant Helm upgrades plus Terraform plan gating for infra changes; 2) preflight snapshotter and ephemeral restore sandbox for smoke-validation without impacting live tenants; 3) safe-revert proxy to route traffic to pre-upgrade control-plane replicas during revert windows while keeping DB migrations immutable; 4) downgrade-guard verifier that scans Helm charts, migration manifests, and image tags to block rollbacks that would produce irreversible schema mismatches; 5) Helm chart hooks and post-upgrade probes to validate operator readiness and tenant-specific healthchecks.

Design notes: the orchestrator uses a declarative ReleaseWave CRD with fields: waveOrder, tenantSelector, preflightChecks, allowPartial (default false). Each wave runs: snapshot -> terraform plan gate (if infra diffs) -> helm upgrade --wait with canary replicas -> run probe suite in ephemeral namespace restored from snapshot -> mark wave success. Revert flow: when a wave is failed or a rollback is requested, the orchestrator triggers the safe-revert proxy and runs a revert plan that updates Ingress/LoadBalancer routing to pre-upgrade control-plane endpoints, scales up the pre-upgrade controller replicas (read-only where necessary), and ensures no down-migrations are applied.

Safety and guarantees: the system intentionally separates network-level rollback from database state, preventing accidental downgrade of DB schema. A checksum manifest pins chart and migration versions for each tenant at release time. Downgrade-guard rejects reverts if checksum mismatches indicate migration reversal would be required. Terraform changes are gated by a plan-quarantine: terraform plan must be approved by the release-runner and is only applied in the wave if the plan is identical to the pre-approved plan.

Backwards compatibility: clusters without the ReleaseWave CRD are unaffected. The safe-revert proxy is an opt-in component that can be installed independently. Helm changes include additive hooks and default to previous behavior when flags are off.

Testing and CI: unit tests for orchestrator reconcile logic, integration tests running small E2E in CI that simulate a two-wave rollout with induced failure to exercise safe-revert path, and a manual validation run against an internal QA private cluster. CI initially failed on linting (helm template warnings) and one e2e flake; fixes applied and checks re-ran.

Rollback playbook (short): 1) open ReleaseWave status and inspect failing wave -> 2) trigger revert action via 'rpi ctl release revert --wave=<n>' -> 3) orchestrator activates safe-revert proxy and routes traffic to pre-upgrade control-plane -> 4) investigate logs/metrics and either re-run wave after fix or perform tenant-level manual migration.

Checklist: [x] ReleaseWave CRD and controller implemented; [x] Helm chart hooks and probe suites; [x] Terraform plan gating integrated; [x] Safe-revert proxy implemented and documented; [x] E2E tests and smoke-run completed; [x] Release notes drafted.

Related work: ties to ENG-2210 (upgrade orchestration) for long-term rollout automation and ENG-2285 (backup/restore sandboxing).

Why unique: unlike prior migrations that relied on global rollbacks, this PR enables phased waves and network-level reversal without destructive DB downgrades, reducing blast radius and improving recovery time for private customers.
commits_summary: 12 commits: initial CRD and controller scaffold; helm hook templates and probe suite; terraform plan-gate integration; safe-revert proxy service and routing logic; checksum manifest and downgrade-guard; CI fixes for helm lint; add e2e test harness; docs and playbook updates.
review_comments: Arjun: Can we avoid scaling extra control-plane replicas in small clusters? Reply (Maya): orchestrator has clusterSize-based thresholds and will fallback to single-node safe proxy mode.

Lucia: The checksum manifest looks good but how do we rotate pinned images for emergency fix? Reply (Maya): the manifest supports emergency-overrides that require two approvers and will be surfaced in the release log.
Evan: I triggered the e2e fail locally, it was due to race on job cleanup. Reply (Maya): added exponential backoff and ensured job ownerrefs are set; re-ran tests.
Ops (comment): please include terraform state-lock verification in the plan gate. Reply (Maya): added state-lock verification step and updated docs.
Lucia (approval): approved pending minor docs tweaks.
